source_text.body:
Use Gemini to plan code and review Claude's output
A user had Gemini think through a coding project, write concise prompts for Claude, and review the code Claude produced.
·
Mar 14, 2026
Done with
GE
Gemini
CL
Claude
What they did
The user used Gemini alongside a Claude Code account on a small coding project: Gemini helped think through the work, turn those ideas into concise prompts for Claude, and review Claude’s code. For one review, they started a fresh Gemini chat, uploaded a zip of the code plus a CLAUDE.md project description, took Gemini’s minor suggestions back to Claude for changes, then uploaded Claude’s tar.gz package to Gemini for a final check before running it.
How it went
The process had been useful for learning, but this review failed badly: Gemini said the code was safe to run and even predicted 758 new vectors, then later admitted the archive had been truncated and it could not fully see the updated indexer.py. The user said that broke their trust in Gemini for code review.
Worth knowing
The key catch was file handling: passing archives through chat led Gemini to silently miss files, so the user and commenters pointed to giving models direct access to the project files instead.
Try it yourself
with
Gemini
Copy prompt
I am building [project description] using [language or framework]. First, help me think through the architecture and break the work into steps, then write a concise, self-contained prompt for each step that I can give to Claude. After I paste back the code Claude produced, review it for bugs, missing requirements, and security problems, and finish with a prioritized list of fixes.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GoogleGeminiAI/comments/1r8igy5/something_happened_yesterday_that_made_me
